mechanism.summary: An award is decided by a bounded electorate that ranks candidates from what it saw, not from true value. The chain starts with who is eligible (rookie status, offence versus defence) and who plays enough to be considered. Production is then measured relative to the peers the voters implicitly compare against, mostly through the counting stats and milestones they remember (yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions) rather than efficiency. Team success acts as a multiplier, strongly for the MVP and the Coach of the Year. The narrative path (hot streak, late-season surge, primetime exposure, injury timing relative to ballots) moves a candidate within the list, and among close candidates the split of votes across teammates and similar profiles decides the plurality. Finally the contract adds mechanics: ballot close, ties paying 1/N, and monthly windows with only a handful of games. Predictions must therefore be of voter behaviour on a candidate set, not of player quality.

stages.name: Eligibility and candidate pool
stages.description: Eligibility defines the pool: rookies for the Rookie awards, offence or defence for the position-split awards, the month window for monthly awards, and any quarterback bias in the MVP. Pool size is small (3 to 8 live candidates for a typical award at the end of the season) and non-uniform: recent history shows that most MVPs are quarterbacks on top seeds, while non-quarterbacks win Offensive Player of the Year.
stages.distribution: Candidate set is a short list; probability mass concentrated on 2-4 names with a long tail of those who need a late surge.

stages.name: Realised production relative to peers
stages.description: Voters see counting statistics and milestones: passing and rushing yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions, receptions, with a lean to visible plays. Production per game and cumulative both count, so injuries trade rate for volume. Production must be compared with the pool of candidates at the same position and across positions for the cross-position awards. Defensive candidates (DPOY, DROY) are scored on a sack, pressure, interception, tackle-for-loss composite and offensive skill candidates on EPA, all ranked within the eligible pool by nfl.position_peer_production_index, with banked totals extended by nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.
stages.distribution: Production totals approximately normal across the season with heavy tails for TDs; ranking relative to peers is what matters, and seasonal rank changes slowly late in the year.

stages.name: Team success multiplier
stages.description: Team record, seed and division title are strong predictors of award votes, especially for the MVP and Coach of the Year: the same stat line earns a vote share depending on the team's seed. The standings simulation gives the distribution of final record and seed, which is a function of the remaining schedule and injuries across the roster.
stages.distribution: Seed distribution is discrete; vote share is a step-like function of seed (top-seed premium) rather than linear in wins.

stages.name: Availability and games-played risk
stages.description: Injury and rest before the ballot date eliminate or discount candidates; an injury after ballots close has no effect. Because games missed have a visible penalty in voting, the probability of playing the remaining games matters in a non-linear way: missing a few games costs far less than missing a month.
stages.distribution: Games-played distribution with a mass at full availability and a left tail; voters apply a penalty that jumps at roughly 3+ missed games (assumption, to be estimated).

stages.name: Narrative, exposure and milestone effects
stages.description: Voters respond to milestones (1,000 yards, 2,000 yards, sack or touchdown records), to national-television performances and to recent games. The distinction between realised and expected production (touchdown luck) matters because voters do not regress, so the luck inflated stat line wins votes even if its true value is lower; the model should predict what voters see.
stages.distribution: Narrative effects are discrete and path dependent: a milestone or record chase produces a jump in the vote probability rather than a gradual change.

stages.name: Vote aggregation: plurality over a panel and vote splitting
stages.description: The winner is the candidate with the most votes from a panel of about 50 voters (for the AP awards, assumption: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), so the win probability is the probability that his share exceeds each rival's in a Dirichlet-like vote model. Similar candidates, especially teammates or same-position rivals, split the same voters' preferences and reduce each other's chance.
stages.distribution: Multinomial vote split with overdispersion; winner probability is a softmax-like function of latent scores with correlated errors among similar candidates.

stages.name: Award-specific drivers: coaches, comebacks and monthly windows
stages.description: Coach of the Year follows the surprise in team wins relative to a pre-season expectation, Comeback Player depends on the severity of the prior-year setback, and monthly awards are decided on four or five games with the bye week removing games from some teams. These contracts need their own sub-model on top of the common chain.
stages.distribution: Window sums over 3-5 games have much higher variance than season totals; coach surprise is approximately normal in wins but selects the top few overachievers.

nfl.award_milestone_proximity.label: Milestone and record proximity for each candidate
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.mechanism: Distance of a candidate's projected final total from round-number or record milestones that voters respond to (e.g. 2,000 rushing yards, 5,000 passing yards, 20 sacks, franchise or league records).
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.rationale: Vote probability is not smooth in production: reaching a milestone adds a discrete narrative bump and a record chase draws attention for several weeks, so award probability has a cliff near thresholds.
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.measurement: For each candidate and award, list milestone totals from the last 15 years of winners' stat lines (the 20th percentile of winners' totals for each key stat as threshold); compute probability that projected final total exceeds each threshold from the season-to-date accrual model (rate x remaining games with games-played risk); feature = P(exceed) and distance in games. Rolls forward after each week; units: probability.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference season stats and award voting history
raw_data: historical AP voting tables with winners' stats
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.why: Captures threshold effects in voting that a smooth production-to-vote function misses, especially for OPOY, DPOY and rookie awards driven by round-number totals.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.label: Teammate and look-alike candidate vote-splitting penalty
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.mechanism: Reduction in a candidate's vote share caused by another strong candidate with the same team, position or narrative.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: Plurality voting splits similar support: two quarterbacks on the same team or two edge rushers with similar sack counts take votes from each other, so independent win probabilities overstate the sum and understate a third candidate's chance.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: From historical AP voting records (last 20 seasons), estimate a Plackett-Luce or Dirichlet model where each candidate's latent score includes a penalty beta x (score of the best same-team or same-position rival); estimate beta by maximum likelihood with candidates having at least one vote; shrink beta toward 0 with a ridge prior (lambda tuned by leave-one-season-out). Output: winner probabilities after the split correction.
raw_data: AP vote shares by candidate-season, team, position
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.why: Needed to make winner probabilities sum to one and to price second-tier candidates on a team that has a front runner.

nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.label: Rookie opportunity: draft capital, starter status and snap/role share
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.mechanism: Draft pick number, starter status in Week 1 and cumulative snap share of rookies, plus team context (quarterback, line) that gives opportunities.
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.rationale: Rookie awards go to rookies who played substantial roles on visible teams; draft capital predicts both opportunity and the voters' prior, and the role is determined by early-season depth charts and injuries ahead of him.
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.measurement: For each rookie: draft pick (log scale), team depth chart rank at the first week's report, snap share and touches or pressures per game over the season, shrunk with k=3 games; feature = expected rest-of-season production given role, based on a regression of final production on first-6-week role and draft slot over 2010-2025 rookies.
free_sources: nflverse draft picks and snap counts
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.why: Defines the viable candidate set and base rates for KXNFLDROTY, KXNFLOROTY, KXNFLROTM and Rookie All-Team, the awards sampled in the rules text.

nfl.award_month_window_games.label: Monthly award window: games, byes and stat accrual inside the calendar window
nfl.award_month_window_games.mechanism: Number of games each candidate's team plays in the contract's calendar month and the candidate's stat production within that window.
nfl.award_month_window_games.rationale: Monthly awards are decided on three to five games, so a team on a bye, a rest day or a Thursday game changes the sample; a candidate with five games has more chances than one with three.
nfl.award_month_window_games.measurement: For each award month, from the league schedule: games per team in the window (3, 4 or 5); expected stats per game from the candidate's role and an opponent adjustment; window total = sum over games; standard deviation scaled by sqrt(games) with game-level variance from the player's last 20 games. Output probability that the candidate leads the window at his position.
nfl.award_month_window_games.why: The October rookie-of-the-month sample contract is decided inside a short window; opportunities vary by bye and the model must use the real game count.

nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.label: Coach surprise: wins above own pre-season expectation
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.mechanism: Team win total minus the expected wins from a pre-season rating built without betting-market inputs (own roster and last-year efficiency prior).
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.rationale: Coach of the Year is a vote for surprise rather than quality, so the relevant measure is outcome minus prior expectation; using a sportsbook win total would import a market price as an input, so the prior must be from the model's own rating.
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.measurement: Pre-season expected wins = sum over remaining games of own win probability from team rating (roster continuity regression of last-year EPA, QB change, strength of schedule); surprise = (projected final wins from standings simulation) - pre-season expected wins; add division title and playoff seed bonuses based on historical winners; units: wins above expectation.
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.why: Gives KXNFLCOTY (and the Comeback/COTY style awards) a quantity that responds to over-performance, which the existing production-based inputs lack.

nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.label: Voter exposure: primetime games, national attention and public straw polls
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.mechanism: Count of primetime and national games for the candidate's team so far and standing in published writers' ballots or straw polls from non-market sources.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.rationale: Voters see the nationally televised games and discuss candidates in public straw polls; this is a signal of voter sentiment distinct from production and is not a market price.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.measurement: Primetime-game counts and share of the candidate's yards or touchdowns in those games to date; rank in published straw polls (e.g. by members of the voting panel) at each week (rank points via Borda). Combined into one score with weights from historical regression on vote share, as-of each Tuesday; no betting prices or Kalshi quotes used.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.why: Provides a voter-behaviour signal without importing prices, helping to distinguish the front runner from candidates with equal production.

nfl.position_peer_production_index.label: Cross-position production index versus peers (offence and defence)
nfl.position_peer_production_index.mechanism: Converts a candidate's season-to-date production into a position-neutral standing among eligible candidates, using EPA-based value for offensive players and a defensive-production composite for defenders.
nfl.position_peer_production_index.rationale: The record's production stage relied on WEAK inputs and one QB-only input, so DPOY, DROY and OPOY (skill positions) had no calibrated production measure. Voters compare a sack leader with a coverage corner, so a within-position percentile is needed; it must also be shrunk for small samples early in the season.
nfl.position_peer_production_index.measurement: Offensive candidates: EPA contributed per game (QB: EPA+CPOE composite from nfl.qb_efficiency; RB/WR/TE: receiving or rushing EPA plus yards over expected per touch) converted to z-score versus the 2015-2025 distribution of the same position at the same week of season. Defenders: composite z of sacks per game, pressures per game (if available) and QB hits, interceptions plus passes defensed, tackles for loss, and forced fumbles with weights 0.35/0.25/0.15/0.15/0.10 (weights are assumptions to be fit to past DPOY vote share); shrink toward position mean with k=5 games; ranks within the eligible pool (rookies only for rookie awards); as-of the last completed week. Output: rank and z-gap to the next candidate.
free_sources: nflverse weekly player stats (sacks, QB hits, interceptions, passes defended, TFL)
raw_data: weekly player stats: player_id, week, position, sacks, qb_hits, def_interceptions, passes_defended, tackles_for_loss, forced_fumbles
nfl.position_peer_production_index.why: Gives DPOY/DROY/OPOY/OROY a production measure that is comparable across positions, instead of the weak award-stats and QB-only fields.

nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.label: Rest-of-season statistical projection to the ballot cutoff
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.mechanism: Projects each candidate's final regular-season totals by adding expected remaining-game production to banked totals, with a games-played hazard.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.rationale: Awards are voted on final-season body of work, and Kalshi prices trade in October to January while about half the games remain; ranking by banked stats ignores that a candidate on a bye or with a tough schedule will fall behind. The projection is for production rank, not a price.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.measurement: Projected total = banked total + sum over remaining games g of P(plays g) x expected per-game rate_g, where the per-game rate is a 50/50 blend of season-to-date per-game rate and a 3-year prior (shrunk with k=6 games), scaled by opponent defence adjustment from nfl.schedule_strength (+-10 percent cap) and by P(plays g) from nfl.games_played_dist; uncertainty from a negative-binomial per-game sd fitted on 2015-2025. As-of: before the next kickoff window; cutoff = last regular-season game (ballot close date assumed at the end of the regular season, unverified, see u3).
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.why: Turns banked production into a projected final production rank, the quantity voters ultimately compare, at the date the contract trades.

nfl.games_played_dist.reason: Missed games before ballots are the main route to eliminating a leading candidate; the penalty is non-linear.

nfl.qb_efficiency.reason: Relevant for MVP and quarterback-dominated awards, but voters weight totals and team success more than efficiency; irrelevant for defensive and non-quarterback awards.

nfl.td_luck.reason: Useful to assess fragility of leaders but voters do not regress, so it predicts reversion of future games rather than votes.

nfl.season_to_date_pace.reason: Accrual plus remaining games defines milestone chances; duplicates the standard season-stat projection.

nfl.schedule_strength.reason: Voters rarely adjust for schedule strength, and remaining strength moves production slightly; weak for the voting process itself.

m.quote_history.reason: The Kalshi price path is market output; it can calibrate narrative momentum after the fact but it is not a driver of the vote.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook award odds are another market price; the draft listed them as a primary input, which would make a model an echo of other odds.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the awarding body, window, eligibility and tie payment; two of the sampled series show different bodies (AP vs league).

nfl.leader_order_statistic.reason: A vote winner is a plurality over a panel's ballots, not the maximum of a statistic; the max-of-N analogue is approximate and misses vote splitting.

nfl.fantasy_points_model.reason: A position-neutral fantasy translation is not what voters use; defensive awards have no fantasy analogue, and the PPR weighting differs from voter preferences.

interactions.mechanism: MVP voters effectively require a top-two seed for quarterbacks: below that line a leading efficiency edge earns little, above it the same edge translates into most of the first-place votes. The effect of production is therefore conditional on the seed distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare winners' seeds historically and fit vote share as a function of production separately for seeded and unseeded candidates.

interactions.mechanism: A record or milestone chase concentrates the narrative when the candidate is on pace with games to spare; missed games reduce both the total and the probability of reaching the threshold, so the milestone effect is conditional on staying healthy through the remaining weeks.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(milestone) with and without injury risk; compare vote-share residuals for candidates who reached versus narrowly missed thresholds.

interactions.mechanism: Candidates with correlated support (same team, same position) have negatively correlated chances of winning, so the joint distribution of winners is not a product of marginals; a rival's collapse benefits his teammate more than the field.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a joint vote model on historical ballots and compare the log-likelihood to independent softmax; test beta > 0.

interactions.mechanism: An injury has a price effect that depends on whether it occurs before or after ballots close and on how many games remain for voters to see; the same news is decisive in Week 14 and irrelevant after the ballot.
interactions.how_to_test: Split news events by weeks before ballot close and measure change in vote share and in market odds as a diagnostic.

interactions.mechanism: Touchdown luck is rewarded by voters only when it is visible: the vote-share boost from touchdown counts above expectation is multiplied by primetime and highlight exposure, so for a low-exposure candidate a lucky touchdown total adds little, while for a high-exposure candidate it adds vote share even though regression predicts it will fade.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress past vote share on td_luck x exposure index (primetime snaps share, straw-poll rank) and test the product term against td_luck and exposure alone.

interactions.mechanism: For a monthly rookie award the chance to be selected is roughly proportional to the number of games in the window times expected production per game, so a high draft slot with a bye in the window can lose to a lower slot with five games.
interactions.how_to_test: Model window outcomes with games in window as an exposure term and test the coefficient against 1.

nonlinearities.shape: step-like: vote share jumps at the first seed or division title and is flat elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: Voter behaviour treats a number-one seed as a qualification, so the expected vote is a step in seed rather than linear in wins.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: nearly no penalty for 1-2 missed games, steep penalty beyond about 3 missed games
nonlinearities.why: A candidate who misses three or more games is often dropped from the ballot, so award probability is not linear in games played.

nonlinearities.shape: cliff near round-number thresholds and records; flat elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: Voters remember totals like 2,000 yards or the single-season sack record, so probability changes sharply across the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: square-root scaling of variance with games in the window, with a mean proportional to games
nonlinearities.why: A 5-game window has a different winner distribution than a 3-game window; ignoring the count mis-estimates the favourite's probability by changing both mean and sd.

contract.settlement_definition: This registered archetype has no live Kalshi series assigned to it in the ledger (its season-stat contracts are filed under rushing_yards, qb_passing_yards, receiving and the fantasy archetype), so there is no rules text to verify. The expected contract is a regular-season-only total at an integer rung (the sibling KXNFLSEASONPASSYDS and KXNFLSEASONRSHYDS series use a half-yard floor_strike on a 'N+' wording), a league or position leader (dead-heat 1/N on ties, as in the weekly-most series) or a head-to-head season comparison. Overtime, playoffs and the statistics source are unstated for this archetype. Consequence: season-total, career, weekly-most and leader tickers that exist today are filed under other archetypes (see series_mapping_issues); until the ledger is corrected, this record's claims about them are conditional on the wording of those series, which is title-only for most.
variants_and_edge_cases: Season thresholds are one-sided and unrefunded in the sibling series (a player who misses the season fails the rung), unlike per-game ladders with a void rule, so games-played risk is a loss and not a refund.

Leader markets resolve over every eligible player in the league and, per the sibling weekly-most rules, tied leaders share 1/N while a non-participant resolves No; the contender set is an open field, not a list of names.
The 2026-27 schedule has 18 weeks with 17 games per team, so the number of remaining games differs by team through byes, and a Week 17-18 rest of clinched starters truncates the final total.
Weekly leaders (a single-game maximum over all players) and season leaders (a cumulative maximum) share the word 'leader' but are different order statistics with very different randomness.

mechanism.summary: A season statistic is the sum over games played of a per-game output, and the contract is decided by three quantities that are separate in kind: how many games the player appears in (a discrete attrition process), what per-game rate he runs at once on the field (a role and efficiency process that is autocorrelated within the season and can switch regimes after an injury, trade or coaching change), and the realised total already banked. For threshold contracts the probability is the chance that banked plus remaining output crosses the rung, which depends on remaining games and the variance of the sum, larger than independent-game variance because of the persistent role state. For leader contracts the question is a maximum over many correlated contenders, where covariance among teammates and shared schedules matters and the open field of unlisted players holds real mass. Late-season rest of clinched teams and weather add a seasonal truncation to the final weeks.

stages.name: Banked total and games remaining
stages.description: Season-to-date output is known, so the forecast begins from the realised accrual and counts the games each team still plays, with byes and the Week 18 finale deciding how many chances remain. The remaining chances are discrete and unevenly spread across contenders: one player with four games left behind another with five changes the leader odds by a visible margin.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the schedule; remaining games are 0 to 17, and early in the season most of the variance is in the not-yet-played games.

stages.name: Availability: games played and attrition
stages.description: Each remaining game has an appearance probability set by injury status, age and position, suspension risk and (late) rest by clinched teams. Attrition is a hazard process with absences clustering across weeks (a hamstring injury costs several games), so the games-played count has a heavy left tail and strong dependence on the current report.
stages.distribution: Discrete count; near-binomial but with clustered absences, so variance exceeds binomial; mass at 0 additional games for players on injured reserve.

stages.name: Role and usage regime across the remaining season
stages.description: The per-game rate depends on a role state (target share, carry share, snap share) which persists but can change when a teammate is hurt, a depth chart is reshuffled, an offensive coordinator is replaced or a player is traded. Regimes are detected late and priced late, so the regime-change hazard widens the distribution beyond what current usage implies.
stages.distribution: Mixture of regimes: stable role with persistent shares plus a small probability of a shift of 20-40 percent in share (assumption), producing season-level variance beyond sum of independent games.

stages.name: Team volume and efficiency conversion
stages.description: Passing and rushing opportunity come from the team's plays and pass rate, and yield from the quarterback and line; touchdown totals regress heavily and so the per-game expected touchdown rate must be separated from the realised one. A quarterback change can reset volume and efficiency for every skill player on the team.
stages.distribution: Per-game output is a compound count with overdispersion; touchdown counts are low-count Poisson-like with strong regression to role-based expectation.

stages.name: Distribution of the remaining sum with persistent state
stages.description: Remaining output is the sum of games with a within-season autocorrelation: good weeks cluster with a stable role and bad weeks with changed role, so the standard deviation of the sum is larger than sqrt(n) times single-game standard deviation. The distribution over games played and rate is a compound mixture rather than a normal.
stages.distribution: Compound with positive intra-season correlation (roughly 0.1-0.3 at the game-rate level, assumption); right-skewed for touchdowns and receptions.

stages.name: Leader order statistic and contender covariance
stages.description: For a leader contract the event is that one player's total exceeds every rival's: the probability depends on the gap, the remaining games and the dispersion of each contender, and on covariance (teammates share volume negatively for rushing, positively for team-level volume), and is not a product of marginals. The field of less-visible contenders carries mass for position-wide leaders.
stages.distribution: Maximum of N correlated heavy-tailed totals; the probability of leading is a steep function of gap divided by remaining-sum standard deviation.

stages.name: Weekly leaders and settlement rules
stages.description: Weekly leader contracts are single-game maxima over the full player pool, so the tail of the per-game distribution and the ties convention (1/N) matter and are completely different from cumulative leader contracts; regular-season-only wording and statistic source decide eligibility.
stages.distribution: Single-game maximum of ~hundreds of players; heavy right tail; dead-heat splitting of ties.

nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.label: Role-regime change hazard (trade, teammate injury, coordinator change)
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.mechanism: Probability per week that a player's share of targets, carries or snaps shifts materially because of an event outside his own performance.
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.rationale: Season projections assume the current role persists; events that rewrite a depth chart or play-calling are the main source of large forecast errors and do not appear in per-game variance.
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.measurement: From 2012-2025 weekly data, define a regime shift as a change of at least 25 percent in a 4-game rolling usage share relative to the prior 4 games; estimate hazard per week by event type (teammate injury, trade, coordinator change, rookie return) with logistic regression, shrunk with k=20 events per type; apply to each contender conditional on the current team state; output expected share distribution (mixture) for the remaining games.
free_sources: nflverse weekly stats, rosters, transactions (roster moves)
raw_data: team transactions and coaching staff changes with dates
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.why: Adds the largest unmodelled variance source for season totals: a 25 percent share change on 8 remaining games moves a season total by far more than game-level noise.

nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.label: Within-season persistence of per-game rate (variance components)
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.mechanism: Decomposition of per-game output variance into a persistent player-season component and a game-level noise component.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.rationale: Season-sum variance is sqrt(n) times game sd only if games are independent; role persistence makes the sum more dispersed, so the probability of reaching distant rungs is larger than an independent model says.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.measurement: For each statistic and position fit a mixed model on 2012-2025 player-games: y_game = u_player-season + e_game, with u from a normal distribution and e from a count distribution; estimate the ratio sigma_u / sigma_e and the ICC by position and stat; apply to project season total variance = n x Var(e) + n^2 x Var(u) over remaining games; use the current-season estimate of u as the posterior mean with shrinkage proportional to games played.
raw_data: player-game stats with player_id, season, week, position
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.why: Provides the correct dispersion for threshold and leader probabilities and is why season-stat rungs are wider than normal-approximation estimates.

nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.label: Clinched-seed rest: expected snap fraction of starters in the final two weeks
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.mechanism: Probability and magnitude of reduced snaps for starters in Week 17-18 when seeds or division titles are clinched.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.rationale: In the final weeks teams with nothing to play for rest key starters, which truncates cumulative totals just when leader races are decided; the effect depends on the coach's history and on the clinch state.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.measurement: For each team, compute the probability of each clinch state by Week 16 from the standings simulation; from 2015-2025, estimate expected snap fraction in Weeks 17-18 for starters by position as a function of state (clinched top seed, clinched any seed, eliminated), coach-specific rest history (shrink with k=2 occasions), and player age; output expected fraction of normal snaps and its distribution.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.why: Cuts the expected games and snaps of the leading contenders in the exact weeks when many leader contracts are decided, which season-to-date pace ignores.

nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.label: Pairwise covariance of remaining output among contenders
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.mechanism: Covariance of remaining-season output between contenders sharing a team, position room or quarterback.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.rationale: Leader probability involves the probability that one exceeds the other, so independence overstates the probability of both being high; teammates' rushing is negatively linked, and passing and receiving of a QB and his top receiver positively.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-seasons, estimate residual correlation between remaining-season output of pairs (same team same stat; QB-WR pairs; RB-RB) after removing season-level means, using the last 8 weeks as the test window; shrink pairwise correlation to the category average with k=30 pairs; use in a multivariate normal or copula simulation of the contender field.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.why: Needed so leader probabilities sum correctly across the field and so a teammate's injury changes the leader odds of another candidate.

nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.label: Distribution of the weekly leader's value by position and statistic
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.mechanism: Baseline distribution of the single-game maximum over all players of a position in a given week and the number of near-miss contenders.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.rationale: The weekly leader market is decided by the top of a very large field; the winner's threshold, not the favourite's mean, sets the chance, and the leader's value is heavy-tailed.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.measurement: For each position and statistic, from 2010-2025 weeks collect the weekly maximum and top-5 values; fit a generalized extreme value distribution by position; condition on number of games in the week (Thursday, Monday, bye-heavy weeks) and weather. Output P(player i is the weekly max) via simulation of the active-player field with player-specific distributions.
raw_data: player-week stats, number of games in the week
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.why: Weekly leader contracts are a different statistical object from season leaders and cannot be priced from the season-to-date pace input.

interactions.mechanism: The season total is the product of a discrete games-played count and a persistent per-game rate, so a high-rate player with a high attrition hazard has a bimodal distribution; moments of the total from independent components understate the left tail and overstate the median.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the total from games and rate jointly versus from independent normal approximations and compare calibration at the 10th and 90th percentiles.

interactions.mechanism: Targets and carries move together after an event: when a teammate is lost, one player's share rises and another's falls, and a coordinator change shifts the pass-run balance for everyone, so the rate is a mixture whose weights are updated by news.
interactions.how_to_test: Detect regime shifts around events and compare usage share before and after, by position.

interactions.mechanism: The expected snaps of starters fall at the point a team clinches a seed (usually Week 16-18) and the effect is concentrated in the last two weeks; before that point pace extrapolation is valid and after it drops.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Weeks 17-18 snap shares of starters on clinched versus unclinched teams.

interactions.mechanism: Leader probability for a player depends on the variance of his lead over each rival: positive covariance between two contenders on one offence (quarterback and a receiver sharing team passing volume) shrinks the variance of their gap so the better one is more reliably ahead, while negative covariance within a backfield (competing for the same carries) widens the gap variance and makes order flips more likely. The sign is positive for same-team passing pairs and negative for same-position teammates.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit leader probabilities from a covariance-matrix simulation versus an independent simulation, and compare Brier score and calibration on historical position leaders, separately for same-team positive-sign and same-position negative-sign pairs.

interactions.mechanism: Banked touchdown excess fades toward the role-based rate only to the extent it came from luck (long scores, fumble-recovery touchdowns); excess that rests on a stable red-zone share persists, and a role-regime change redefines the role-based rate itself, so the shrinkage of banked touchdowns toward expectation depends on how stable the underlying role is.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress remaining touchdowns on banked touchdowns, role-based expectation and an indicator of red-zone share stability or a regime-change event; test the banked x stability term and the null that banked excess has no effect.

interactions.mechanism: The weekly leader's probability depends on the tail of a player's single-game distribution rather than on its mean, so two players with equal means can differ several-fold in leader probability; this effect is a function of the tail index.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare weekly-leader frequency among players by tail-heaviness (95th percentile over mean) controlling for mean.

nonlinearities.shape: bounded and left-skewed: total increases linearly with games but the probability of a rung drops steeply when the required games approach the games remaining
nonlinearities.why: A threshold requiring almost every remaining game at an above-average rate becomes very sensitive to a single missed game, so the rung probability is nonlinear near the feasible limit.

nonlinearities.shape: sigmoid in the standardized gap (lead divided by remaining-sum standard deviation), saturating near 0 and 1
nonlinearities.why: A lead of one standard deviation yields only about 84 percent, while a two-sd lead yields 98 percent, so leader odds change quickly in the middle range and slowly in the tails.

nonlinearities.shape: shrinkage toward the role-based mean: realised touchdown excess decays with remaining games
nonlinearities.why: Banked touchdown luck does not carry into remaining games, so the extrapolated total regresses by a factor that depends on how many games remain.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy right tail: extreme-value shape parameter above zero for yards and fantasy points
nonlinearities.why: The weekly leader has a distribution with a long tail, so very high weekly leader values are more likely than normal-extreme extrapolation implies.

contract.settlement_definition: Season-structure futures settle on the final 2026-27 regular season or postseason outcome: team win totals and exact wins (KXNFLWINS-*, KXNFLEXACTWINS*), division and seed contracts (e.g. KXNFL1SEED YES if the team is the #1 seed in its conference at the end of the regular season), round qualification (KXNFLROUNDQUAL for the divisional round), the exact championship pairing (KXNFLSBOUTCOME), the first overall pick team (KXNFLDRAFT1ST resolves to whichever team ultimately makes the pick) and combos (KXNFLPLAYOFFC both teams in the playoffs, KXNFLNBA cross-league champions). A tie is not a loss for undefeated-in-division wording; how ties are counted in win totals is not stated in any sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is the #1 seed in the National Football Conference at the conclusion of the 2026-2027 Pro Football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The seed contract settles on the final regular-season seed after all tiebreakers, so it is a function of the full standings and the league's tiebreak procedure, not of the playoff results.

rules_evidence.quote: A tie (game result) does not count as a loss.
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties exist as a distinct game result and are treated as not-a-loss for the undefeated-in-division contract; a division record of 5-0-1 resolves YES, so tie probability affects this contract directly.

rules_evidence.quote: If either team is eliminated from contention for its specified role, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: The exact-pairing contract is a joint event over both conference champions and the final result, resolving No as soon as either team is eliminated, so its probability is a product of correlated bracket paths.

rules_evidence.quote: the market will resolve to Yes for the team that ultimately makes the selection, not the team that originally held the pick
rules_evidence.establishes: First-overall-pick contracts follow ownership of the pick at the draft, so pick trades and tanking decisions matter alongside record and strength-of-schedule tiebreaks.

rules_evidence.quote: If the New York J Pro Football team ceases to exist, permanently relocates
rules_evidence.establishes: Multi-year streak-ending contracts carry franchise-existence clauses and a horizon of several seasons, a different process from one-season win totals.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLWINS-* (per team over/under) and KXNFLEXACTWINS* (exact count) have title-only entries in the sample; whether a tie counts as half a win, zero or is excluded is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, and ties matter at 9.5-win lines with roughly a 0.2 percent per-game tie rate.

KXNFLSBOUTCOME (exact winner and runner-up) and KXNFLPLAYOFFC (both teams make playoffs) are joint events: for same-conference or same-division pairs the events are negatively correlated through zero-sum games, for different conferences close to independent.
KXNFLNBA joins an NFL title to an NBA title (status inactive in the sample) and is a product of two independent league outcomes; the NFL leg alone defines the football information needed.

Regular-season contracts (seed, win totals, division) are fixed at the end of Week 18 under the league's tiebreaker rules, while KXNFLROUNDQUAL and the pairing market depend on the playoff bracket and reseeding; KXNFLENDSTREAK spans several future seasons.

The set includes league-level aggregates such as division with most wins, single-season record broken, team wins by week and playoff host markets; none have rules text, so their definitions are unknown.
contract.settlement_data_source: The sampled texts refer to the league's regular-season standings and the 'Governing League' official tiebreak methodology (named in the sibling division-order series); no explicit data vendor is stated.

mechanism.summary: Season outcomes are produced by a hierarchical process. Each team has a latent strength with real uncertainty at the start of the season (the prior is a blend of last-year performance, roster continuity and quarterback change, regressed hard toward the league mean) that is learned slowly from games, and that shared uncertainty acts on every game the team plays, making win totals more dispersed than independent games would give. Each game's win probability is a function of rating difference, home field, rest, and the availability of the quarterback and a handful of other key players, which are random across the season and correlated within a team. Win totals aggregate 17 such games, ties are possible, and standings follow from all teams' results through the league's tiebreakers, where division games are zero-sum and who plays whom decides leverage. Seeds give a bye only to the top seed, and playoff single elimination turns seed and full-strength roster into title odds. Cross-market consistency then follows from the same simulated worlds.

stages.name: Latent team strength with persistent uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's latent strength enters every game and is updated by results; early in the season most of the uncertainty is the shared prior error, which does not average out across 17 games. The prior combines previous efficiency (regressed), roster continuity, quarterback change and coaching change, and the posterior is revised by opponent-adjusted performance with luck-related components removed.
stages.distribution: Normal prior on rating (sd about 1.5-2.5 points of spread at the preseason, assumption) updating toward a smaller posterior sd; the shared error induces correlation between a team's game results.

stages.name: Key-player availability, especially the quarterback
stages.description: The quarterback accounts for a larger share of team strength than any other player, and his missed games change the whole team's rating for those games; other key players (edge, tackle, cornerback) matter less. Injuries are a random process across the season with clustering, and the drop to the backup depends on who the backup is.
stages.distribution: Mixture across scenarios: QB1 plays all games (about 70% of teams), misses 1-4 games, or misses a large block; rating shift of several points between QB1 and backup, team-specific.

stages.name: Game-level win probability and schedule
stages.description: For each remaining game win probability is a logistic function of the rating difference plus home field and rest/travel, and the schedule composition determines both the expected wins and the leverage. Ties can occur, contributing half-win in standings and a not-lost result in some contracts.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with probability in roughly 0.1-0.9; ties ~0.2-0.3% per game; outcomes conditionally independent given ratings and availability.

stages.name: Win-total aggregation and exact-win distribution
stages.description: The number of wins is the sum of game outcomes, with variance larger than the binomial because of shared rating uncertainty and correlated availability. Exact-win and threshold contracts need the full probability mass function, and a 9.5 line is much more sensitive to the tails than to the mean.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed Poisson-binomial with sd approximately 2.0-2.4 wins; exact-win probabilities peak around 15-20 percent at the mean.

stages.name: Standings, tiebreakers and zero-sum leverage
stages.description: Division and seed contracts are determined jointly: division games produce a winner and a loser, so a team's chance depends on rivals' results, and ties at the same record are resolved by the league's tiebreak ladder (head-to-head, division record, common opponents, strength of victory and others). Games between direct competitors are more informative than other games.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution across all 32 teams' win totals with negative correlation among division rivals; tiebreak resolution is a deterministic function of full results.

stages.name: Seed, bye and bracket path to title
stages.description: Only the top seed receives a bye, and seed determines home field and opponent strength; the title contract is the product of three or four game win probabilities in a reseeded bracket where roster health at playoff time matters and regular-season rest games distort the rating. Playoff win probabilities use a full-strength rating rather than season-average.
stages.distribution: Product of 3-4 correlated game probabilities; convex in seed because of the bye; title odds heavy-tailed across the top teams.

stages.name: Special futures: first pick, undefeated, streaks and combos
stages.description: The first pick follows the bottom of the standings plus the strength-of-schedule tiebreak and any traded picks; undefeated and win-streak contracts depend on the maximum of correlated runs of wins; combos multiply independent leagues. These need their own simulation outputs rather than only win totals.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value style: worst record among 32 teams, longest streak across 32 teams, plus ownership of pick (discrete).

talent_strength.note: Rating with uncertainty and playoff-time full-strength rating; the ratings input mixes market-implied history, which must be removed.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent strength and the matchups among direct rivals.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and replacement quality dominate role effects at the team level.

availability_news.note: Injury vintages and scenario tree for the quarterback.

coaching_scheme.note: Head-coach and coordinator changes are part of the preseason prior but have no specified quantity; the effect of a new play-caller on team win expectation is not defined in the catalog.

environment.note: Venue and weather matter in single games but their season-level effect on win totals is small and symmetric across teams, except through home-field and dome versus outdoor schedules already in the rating and rest inputs.

game_context_script.note: Seed and bracket path define playoff game contexts; in-game script is not relevant at season level.

pace_volume.note: Season-level wins are not driven by a count of opportunities such as plays or possessions as a modelling stage; pace enters only through the rating's efficiency measures.

efficiency_conversion.note: Close-game and takeaway luck removal from ratings.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed win totals and joint division outcomes.

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not alter season outcomes beyond what is already captured in the team's results; the tiebreaker rules are the relevant rule set and are included under standings.

settlement_contract.note: Tie counting for win totals remains unresolved; seed and pairing contracts are defined in the rules.

nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.label: Shared team-rating uncertainty (posterior sd) carried across all games
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's latent rating, applied as a common draw across all of that team's games in a simulation.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.rationale: If every game is simulated at a fixed rating, win totals are too concentrated and tail probabilities for 4-win or 13-win teams are underestimated; the shared error is the main reason season win-total distributions are wider than binomial.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.measurement: Prior sd = 2.2 points of rating at the preseason (calibrated by backtest of preseason ratings against final results over 2002-2025; estimate sd from residuals); posterior sd after n games = 1/sqrt(1/prior_sd^2 + n/s2) with game-level residual sd s2 = 13.5 points; sample a team-level draw per simulation and keep it across all games. Output: sd by team and week.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.why: Controls tail mass of wins and playoff probabilities in the season simulation, which the current catalog states as 'with uncertainty' without a defined quantity.

nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.label: Team-specific quarterback scenario tree and rating drop to the backup
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.mechanism: Expected loss in team rating, in points, when the starting quarterback is replaced by the depth-chart backup, and the probability distribution of missed games.
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.rationale: Quarterback change is the largest swing in team rating, and the size of the drop varies from one point for teams with a competent backup to ten points for teams with a replacement-level one.
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.measurement: For each team, rating drop = (QB1 value - QB2 value) in points, where QB value = career-regressed EPA per dropback prior x dropbacks x conversion (about 0.2 points of margin per 0.01 EPA per dropback per game, from regression), shrunk to league mean with k=300 dropbacks; missed-game distribution from historical QB games missed by age and injury history (negative binomial); scenario tree: QB1 all games, partial, absent. Output expected wins lost and a distribution.
raw_data: QB dropbacks and EPA by player
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.why: Directly converts quarterback availability into a team win distribution, which the current catalog treats as a flag.

nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.label: Direct-competitor leverage: remaining games among teams contending for the same slots
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.mechanism: Matrix of remaining games between teams whose division or wild-card outcomes are linked, with each game's swing in the target contract's probability.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.rationale: Games among rivals are zero-sum for the division and seed contract, so they move probabilities by roughly twice as much as other games, and the head-to-head tiebreaker also locks in earlier results.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.measurement: In each weekly simulation, for each remaining game compute the change in P(contract) between simulated worlds where each team wins (leverage = |P(win)-P(loss)| x game probability uncertainty); aggregate to team-level remaining leverage by division and wild-card group; add head-to-head results to date as first-tiebreak state. Output: leverage score per game and per team.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.why: Explains why division and seed contracts are not functions of expected wins alone and identifies when a single rival game decides the contract.

nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.label: Full-strength playoff rating versus season-average rating
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.mechanism: Team rating computed on games with the current starting lineup (healthy QB, lines, defence) excluding games with rested starters or garbage time.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.rationale: Regular-season averages include injuries that have healed and rested-starter games in Weeks 17-18, which bias the rating used for playoffs and title futures.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.measurement: Compute opponent-adjusted efficiency (EPA/play margin) over games where the current starting QB and at least 80 percent of current starters (by snap weight) played, excluding Week 18 rested-starter games and fourth-quarter garbage time (win probability >95 percent); shrink to the season average with k=5 games; output rating in points of margin and the difference from season average as an adjustment for playoff-round probabilities.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.why: Title and round-qualification futures depend on playoff-time strength, not on the average over games with a different lineup.

nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.label: First-overall-pick race: bottom of standings, strength-of-schedule tiebreak and pick ownership
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.mechanism: Distribution of the team that ultimately makes the first pick, from the worst-record contest with its tiebreak and from ownership of traded picks.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.rationale: The first-pick contract depends on who has the worst record, the tiebreak for ties (strength of schedule rather than team strength) and whether the pick has been traded, so it is an extreme-value problem of losing, not winning.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.measurement: Simulate final records, take the minimum-wins team with the league's draft-order tiebreak (lower strength of schedule gets the higher pick, as an assumption flagged SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), then map the draft slot owner via a table of traded picks; add a small tanking adjustment (reduced win probability for teams eliminated by Week 12, estimated from history).
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.why: The sampled KXNFLDRAFT1ST rules state that the team making the selection resolves YES, and none of the other inputs model the loser race or pick ownership.

nfl.standings_sim.reason: The simulation is the structure of every contract here, but its value depends on shared rating error, QB scenarios and tiebreak fidelity, none of which the entry specifies.

nfl.ratings.reason: Mixes own power ratings with market-implied strength history; market-implied components are a benchmark and should not enter an independent model, so only own-rating series are valid.

nfl.roster_continuity.reason: Regresses the preseason prior by returning production; matters early in the season and fades with games played.

nfl.schedule_strength.reason: Opponent strength sets expected wins, but remaining strength must come from current ratings; the previous-season record is stale.

nfl.pythag_luck.reason: Close-game luck regression corrects overstated records; modest effect after games played accumulate.

nfl.turnovers.reason: Takeaway luck inflates records; only a small adjustment to ratings and overlaps with efficiency.

nfl.qb.reason: Quarterback status and replacement quality are the largest team-level swing and need scenarios, not a flag.

nfl.games_played_dist.reason: Key-player absence distribution widens win distributions; duplicated partly by the QB scenario input but relevant for other positions.

nfl.injuries_pit.reason: Current injuries and return dates adjust near-term ratings; timestamps matter most for in-season futures.

nfl.bracket_path.reason: Seed, bye and path are central for conference, title and round-qualification contracts.

nfl.motivation_seeding.reason: Late-season rest and incentives affect the last weeks and the ratings used for playoffs; small for most teams.

nfl.rest_travel.reason: Bye and short-week effects change game probabilities by a point or less; low value as a season-level input.

nfl.futures_coherence.reason: Coherence across linked prices is derived from market quotes; logical constraints are useful for checks but the coherence value does not inform the outcome.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures are a vig-heavy benchmark; using them as a primary input makes the model an echo, though they are a legitimate comparison target.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price drift shows how fast the market reacts but carries no independent information about team strength.

m.rules_text.reason: Determines tie counting, pick ownership, elimination wording and pairing semantics; needed because the same simulation maps to different payoffs.

m.volume_oi.reason: Open interest and volume describe liquidity and carry no information about win totals.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trade history is a market record and would leak prices into the inputs of a season simulation.

nfl.season_sim_distribution.reason: Same simulation viewed through its output distribution; keep one season simulation and read its distribution rather than listing both.

interactions.mechanism: A shared draw of team strength is applied to every game, so uncertainty scales the whole win total and produces dispersion greater than independent games; the effect is largest for the contracts at the tails (4-win, 13-win lines), and shrinks as the season progresses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare win-total dispersion in simulations with and without shared draws against 2002-2025 actual spread of wins around preseason expectation.

interactions.mechanism: The cost of a quarterback's missed games depends on who the games are against: a miss in a division rival game costs more in a tied race and in a weak week of the schedule costs little, so the timing of absence interacts with schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the same absence in different weeks and measure the change in playoff probability.

interactions.mechanism: Division outcomes are zero-sum: a rival's win is a loss for another contender, so probabilities of division titles across four teams are negatively correlated and sum to one; late-season motivation changes the leverage once a team is clinched or eliminated.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare division-winner probabilities from a joint simulation with independent probabilities and measure the sum-to-one error.

interactions.mechanism: Title probability is convex in seed because only the top seed receives a bye and home field, and convex in full-strength rating because a team must win three or four games in a row; a small rating edge compounds across rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate title probability by seed and rating bucket using historical playoffs.

interactions.mechanism: Teams with a record better than their point differential imply an inflated rating that regresses, but regression is strongest early and for teams with a larger uncertainty on rating; the shrinkage should be conditioned on the posterior sd.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress second-half win rate on first-half record and point differential, interacted with games played.

interactions.mechanism: Once a team is eliminated from the playoffs it may lose more often (tanking incentives, starters rested), a regime change that influences the worst-record race but not the playoff contracts.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare win rates of eliminated teams in the last six weeks to ratings-based expectation.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped: playoff probability rises steeply from about 8 to 11 expected wins and flattens outside
nonlinearities.why: The qualification threshold lies in the middle of the win distribution, so a change of one expected win moves playoff probability by 15-20 points near 9 wins and by a few points at 5 or 13 wins.

nonlinearities.shape: step: the top seed receives a bye and the other six seeds do not
nonlinearities.why: A step function in seed distinguishes the number-one seed from the rest, so the title probability rises discontinuously and a team's expected wins only partly determines it.

nonlinearities.shape: mixture: a discrete loss of several rating points with probability equal to the chance of the miss
nonlinearities.why: The quarterback's absence shifts team rating by a lump, so the rating is a mixture rather than a normal, and the win distribution has a heavier left tail for teams with weak backups.

nonlinearities.shape: variance of the win total grows with the square of games played times rating variance
nonlinearities.why: The shared error contributes quadratically to the variance of wins, so it dominates binomial variance by season end for a given rating uncertainty.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNFLTEAMTOTAL settles YES when the named team's final score in the named game exceeds the strike (floor_strike 7.5 for 'over 7.5'), a ladder of half-point rungs on one team's points. KXNFLBOTH settles YES when both teams each score at least a threshold (35 in the sample) and states that overtime points count; a postponed game that starts within 48 hours remains open, otherwise fair price. The KXNFLTEAMTOTAL sample is silent on overtime and on the data source, so whether team-total rungs include overtime points is not established by its own rules text.

rules_evidence.quote: If Minnesota scores over 7.5 points in the Buffalo vs Minnesota Pro Football game originally scheduled for Nov 9, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The contract is a strict over on one team's final score with a half-point strike, so a team score of exactly 8 is YES and the settled quantity is the team's points, not combined or margin.

rules_evidence.quote: Points scored in overtime count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The joint 'both teams reach N' contract explicitly includes overtime scoring; by contrast the team-total ladder text does not say, so the overtime treatment of KXNFLTEAMTOTAL has to be treated as unresolved.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is not started within 48 hours, the market will resolve to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement beyond 48 hours voids to fair price while a delay inside it stays open on the official result; the same wording is absent from the sampled team-total text.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLTEAMTOTAL has only an over-strike ladder sampled (floor_strike 7.5, 'MIN8'); the ladder extends across many rungs of one variable, and low rungs near 7.5 are driven by the chance of a shutdown rather than offense quality.
KXNFLBOTH (both teams at least 35) is a joint tail event across two teams' scores, strongly dependent on game total and pace, not a team-total product of marginals.

Points include non-offensive scores (interception and fumble returns, kick returns, safeties credited to the scoring team), so a team's offence is not the only source; the contract is about the scoreboard, not offensive points.

Overtime handling for KXNFLTEAMTOTAL is not stated; in regular-season overtime (one 10-minute period, sudden death modified) a tied game adds roughly 0.5-1 point to each team's expected total, and the effect is conditional on a tied regulation.

Team scores cluster at 3 and 7 multiples, so rungs on the half-point such as 17.5, 20.5 and 23.5 correspond to different integer score masses and the same-sized gap in mean moves the probability by different amounts.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the sampled text; official game result by the league scoreboard is implied. Two-point conversions and extra points count as points in the final score by standard scoring.

mechanism.summary: A team's final score is the sum of points from a discrete sequence of possessions plus rare non-offensive scores. The number of possessions is set by both offences' tempo and style, the result of each possession is a discrete lottery over touchdown, field goal, no score and turnover with the points of 7 (or 6 or 8), 3, 0 and a chance of opponent return score, and the probabilities depend on starting field position, own offence against the opponent's defence, personnel and weather. Coach decision rules (go for it versus kick, one versus two points) change the points attached to a stalled drive. The score path then rewrites late possessions: leaders run clock, trailers throw and score faster. Because the discrete clusters at 3 and 7 are dense, the response of rung probability to the mean is lumpy and the correct object is the whole score distribution, not a mean plus normal noise.

stages.name: Possessions available to this offence
stages.description: The count of own possessions comes from combined pace, rushing share and clock use of both teams, penalties, turnovers (which add possessions) and the half-end structure; it is typically 10-13 drives per team, and the opponent's ball-control style removes possessions from this offence. A slow, run-heavy opponent cuts this team's chances in a way that own pace alone misses.
stages.distribution: Drives per team per game roughly 9-14 (sd ~1.5); correlated with the opponent's drive count and with game script.

stages.name: Drive start position and field-position inputs
stages.description: Where drives start (after kickoffs, punts, turnovers, returns) determines the expected points per drive, as does the quality of special teams. Turnovers by the opponent give short fields and high scoring chances, so the distribution of start positions reflects both defence and special-teams play.
stages.distribution: Starting yard line ~ distribution centred at the 27-30 yard line with a right tail of short fields after takeaways.

stages.name: Drive outcome lottery: touchdown, field goal, no score
stages.description: Each drive ends in a touchdown with probability that depends on the team's offence, the matchup with defence (pass rush, coverage, run front) and red-zone efficiency, in a field goal when drives stall inside kicker range, or in no points. The points per drive distribution is discrete and the team's total is a convolution across drives.
stages.distribution: Drive points take values 0, 3, ~7 with probabilities ~ 0.65, 0.12-0.15, 0.20-0.25 (league average assumption); sum over ~11 drives gives a discrete distribution with clusters.

stages.name: Kicker and fourth-down decision rules
stages.description: On stalled drives the coach decides to kick or go for it, and the kicker's accuracy by distance and weather decides the three points; changes in 4th-down aggressiveness convert a 3-point outcome into a 0 or 7 gamble. The extra point and two-point decisions add a variance term of about 0.5-1 point per touchdown.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes with decision-dependent probabilities; FG make probability falls from ~95% at 30 yd to ~65% at 55 yd.

stages.name: Personnel availability and offensive-line health
stages.description: The starting quarterback, line and skill players determine the offence's rate; a backup quarterback behind a weak line can reduce the team's expected score by 4-7 points. These status changes arrive late and are partially known at kickoff, and can happen in-game.
stages.distribution: Mixture over personnel scenarios with a heavy shift for the quarterback scenario; in-game injuries produce a smaller shift.

stages.name: Weather, score path and non-offensive scoring
stages.description: Wind and cold reduce passing and field goals, and a blowout compresses the leader's late scoring while the trailer's passing yields more. In addition, the team's defence and special teams can score directly (pick-six, return touchdowns, safeties), adding points independent of its offence, and the opponent's equivalent scores add to the opponent's total but also end the team's drives.
stages.distribution: Defensive/special-teams touchdowns occur in ~10-12% of team games (assumption); weather effects scale with wind above ~15 mph.

stages.name: Discrete score distribution and ladder mapping
stages.description: The team total's rungs are nested events of the same discrete variable; key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14, 17 and so on make the cumulative distribution step-like, and the joint with the opponent's total (both teams at 35) is a tail of the score-pair distribution. The model has to produce the integer probability mass function and read rungs from it, with overtime included or excluded as the rules say.
stages.distribution: Discrete multi-modal distribution; the rung probability from a smooth normal approximation is biased by 2-4 points near key numbers.
