nfl.drive_result_lattice.label: Drive-result lattice: touchdown, field goal, turnover, punt probabilities by start position
nfl.drive_result_lattice.mechanism: Per-drive probabilities of touchdown, field goal and no score for this offence against this defence conditioned on starting field position and game state.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.rationale: Team points are the convolution of drive outcomes, not a smooth function of EPA per play: two offences with equal EPA can have different touchdown-to-field-goal mixes, and the mixture decides the cluster of the score.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.measurement: From drive-level play-by-play 2016-2025 estimate multinomial logit of drive result on start yard line, offence rating, defence rating, down-and-distance style, with team-level random effects (shrink team deviations with k=10 drives); output P(TD), P(FG), P(none) for each of 11 drives by start-position distribution and compute the discrete points distribution by convolution including 2-point and XP outcomes.
raw_data: drive: start_yard_line, result, points, posteam, defteam, plays, time
nfl.drive_result_lattice.why: Creates the discrete team-score distribution that the team total ladder needs and replaces a mean times variance approximation.

nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.label: Fourth-down go-for-it versus field-goal decision rate and two-point policy
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.mechanism: Coach-specific probability of going for it on fourth down by field position and distance, and of attempting a two-point conversion.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.rationale: The decision converts a stalled drive into 3 points, 0 points or 7 points; aggressive coaches raise the variance and shift the mean of team totals, and two-point attempts change points per touchdown.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.measurement: For each head coach over 3 seasons: P(go | yard line bin, distance bin, score and time bin), shrink to model-based optimum with k=15 decisions; two-point attempts per touchdown shrunk with k=10; expected points per stalled drive = P(go) x [conv x 7 + (1-conv) x 0] + (1-P(go)) x P(make FG | distance) x 3; output delta in expected points per game and variance. As-of last completed game.
raw_data: pbp: down, ydstogo, yardline_100, play_type, field_goal_result, two_point_attempt
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.why: Alters the mean and variance of the points associated with the same drive state, and is a coaching feature absent from this archetype's inputs.

nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.label: Non-offensive scoring rate: defensive and special-teams points for and against
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Expected points per game from interception returns, fumble returns, kick and punt return touchdowns and safeties credited to the team, and the equivalent against it.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These points enter the team's total independent of offence, and when scored against the team they end drives; ignoring them biases rungs low for teams with opportunistic defences.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team, count of defensive and special-teams scoring plays per game over the last 25 games with half-life 12, shrunk heavily toward league (k=40 games) because these events are rare; split into takeaway-driven part (own takeaway rate x return-score probability) and special-teams part; opponent's rate against the team computed symmetrically. Output expected points and probability of at least one such score.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play (touchdown with td_team differing from posteam, safety flag)
raw_data: pbp: td_team, posteam, interception, fumble_lost, return_touchdown, safety
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.why: Directly adds a team-total source that the offence-only inputs omit and shifts the lower rungs through the chance of scoring without the offence.

nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.label: Opponent ball-control denial: expected drives and time removed from this offence
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.mechanism: How much the opponent's time of possession, run share and clock usage cut this offence's number of drives relative to its neutral pace.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.rationale: A team's own tempo says nothing about drives if the opponent holds the ball; the effect depends on the matchup of styles and is not captured by pace alone.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.measurement: For each opponent compute average seconds per play, run rate in neutral situations and drive length over the last 12 games (half-life 6); expected own drives = league drives x (own-share model) where own share = own pace / (own pace + opponent pace) adjusted by a regression on historical game drive counts; output expected drives for each side and variance. As-of last game.
raw_data: pbp: drive, posteam, game_seconds_remaining, play_clock info
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.why: Gives the possession count its two-sided structure, which the existing own-pace input lacks.

nfl.team_total_split.reason: Splits the game spread and total into team means, so it is market-derived by construction; it is a benchmark for the rung, not an independent input, and should be compared against own team means.

nfl.off_epa.reason: The team's opponent-adjusted offence is the main driver; per-play EPA must be turned into drive outcomes rather than treated as points.

nfl.def_epa.reason: Opponent defensive efficiency; heavily overlaps coverage_scheme, run_defense and pass_rush, which decompose it.

nfl.pace.reason: Own pace sets plays but not drives; only one side of the possession count.

nfl.drives.reason: Drives are the opportunities for scoring, but need the opponent's ball control, added as a separate input.

nfl.redzone.reason: Red-zone touchdown rate is noisy and regresses; stronger when combined with drive-start data.

nfl.kicker.reason: Accuracy by distance and range converts stalled drives into 3 points, affecting key-number masses; modest in total expected points.

nfl.qb.reason: Starter status is the dominant availability driver of an offence's score; resolves late.

nfl.ol.reason: Line health shifts sack and run-block rates; partial pregame and overlapped by quarterback scenario.

nfl.skill_avail.reason: Missing receivers and backs reduce the ceiling; effect size depends on replacement quality.

nfl.field_pos.reason: Starting field position and special teams change points per drive; correlated with turnovers.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Wind and cold reduce passing and long field goals; style-dependent, thresholded.

nfl.script.reason: Lead and trail effects on late scoring; for team totals the leader's late scoring compresses and the trailer's rises.

nfl.score_resid.reason: Key-number mass at 3 and 7 is genuine structure, but the entry defines residuals around market lines, which should be rebuilt around the model's own mean.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook team totals are the comparison price for the rung, not a physical input; the draft marked it primary.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Rungs of a single team's points are nested and must be monotone and consistent with game total and spread; a constraint, not information.

m.volume_oi.reason: Trading volume and open interest say nothing about how many points a team scores.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trade history is market output; using it as an input makes the model circular.

nfl.coverage_scheme.reason: Coverage shell is a component of the opposing pass defence already summarised in defensive EPA; keep only as a decomposition when available.

nfl.run_defense.reason: Run-defence quality is the rush component of defensive EPA; a separate input double counts the same opponent strength.

nfl.pass_rush.reason: Pass-rush pressure is a driver inside the defensive pass component; as a separate input it repeats the same opponent measurement.

interactions.mechanism: A pass-heavy offence is hurt more by a strong pass defence and a run-heavy one by a strong run defence, and the script chooses which side the offence leans on, so the opponent effect on points depends on the offence's style mixture and the expected score state.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact pass-defence and run-defence ratings with the offence's neutral pass rate in a points-per-drive regression.

interactions.mechanism: In wind or cold the effective kicking range shrinks by 5-10 yards, and a coach who would kick from 48 yards goes for it, which changes the expected points of stalled drives from 2.4 to a 0 or 7 gamble; the decision flips at a threshold distance that depends on weather.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate go-for-it probability and make rate by yard-line bin split by wind; test threshold shifts.

interactions.mechanism: Total points are a convolution over a random number of drives, and the number of drives is correlated with drive outcomes (long touchdown drives remove possessions, quick scores add them), so independent treatment of drive count and outcomes understates the dispersion.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated team total variance with realised variance, using independent and joint draws of drives and outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback behind a weak line and a thin receiver room compounds: pressure rises, completion probability falls and yards after catch fall, so the points loss is greater than the sum of single-position losses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare scoring in games with combined absences versus single absences, controlling for opponent.

interactions.mechanism: The probability mass at key totals (3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 14) depends on the touchdown versus field-goal split, so rung probabilities move discontinuously as the red-zone touchdown rate or the kicker accuracy changes the mixture even if the mean points are constant.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the score pmf with a mixture model and test the change in P(total >= 17) with fixed mean but varying TD/FG mixture.

interactions.mechanism: Non-offensive scores arrive more often when the opponent is trailing and passing (more interceptions) so the team's total gets a lift in precisely the game states where its offence is conservative; the contribution is conditional on opponent script.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate return-score frequency by opponent score state and pass rate.

nonlinearities.shape: lumpy: rung probability changes in steps around the key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24
nonlinearities.why: The score distribution has probability mass concentrated on multiples of 3 and 7, so a shift in the mean moves P(over 13.5) and P(over 16.5) by different amounts rather than smoothly.

nonlinearities.shape: steep decay of make probability beyond about 50 yards, and decision threshold at about 50-55 yards for go-for-it
nonlinearities.why: Field-goal accuracy decays nonlinearly with distance, and coaches switch policies at a similar distance, so points per drive near the 35-yard line is a nonlinear function of range.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold effects near 15 mph wind and near freezing temperature on kicking and deep passing
nonlinearities.why: Wind affects long field goals and deep passes sharply above a threshold, so team points fall in a step-like pattern in wind speed.

nonlinearities.shape: concave for the leader: points per late drive fall as the lead grows because of clock-killing runs, convex for the trailer
nonlinearities.why: A large lead reduces the leader's late scoring chance even as expected margin increases, so team total for a favourite is not monotone in the spread.

contract.settlement_definition: All eleven series settle on Sleeper's full-PPR fantasy points: per-game thresholds and ladders on one player-game (including overtime, no rounding, post-expiration corrections ignored, non-players and unrated players score 0), season totals and season H2H (non-players scored as 0 points, equal totals pay 50 percent), 'any single game' highs, weekly and period leaders, top-N positional ranks (dead-heat 1/N at the cutoff) and fantasy-playoff (Weeks 15-17) leaders that exclude defence, kickers and IDP. The scoring formula is Sleeper's default and the ranking group membership is fixed by Sleeper at expiration.

rules_evidence.quote: Players who do not play or are not assigned a fantasy-point value by Sleeper are treated as scoring 0 fantasy points.
rules_evidence.establishes: A non-participant is a zero, not a void, so availability risk is a real loss on this contract and on the over rungs, and the per-game distribution has an atom at 0.

rules_evidence.quote: The fantasy-point total published by Sleeper at expiration is used, with no additional rounding, and corrections after expiration are not considered.
rules_evidence.establishes: The source of truth is Sleeper's number at expiration, so stat-correction timing and Sleeper's own scoring conventions (not the league's stat sheet) determine settlement; strikes with decimals (9.2) exist.

rules_evidence.quote: rounded to the nearest $0.01 with $0.005 rounded up
rules_evidence.establishes: The ladder is a scalar at $0.01 per point, rounded half up, capped at $1.00 (100 points), so its fair value is the truncated mean and not a tail probability.

rules_evidence.quote: If either player does not play in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season they will be treated as having scored 0 points.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season H2H treats a missing season as a zero total and ties pay 50 percent, so the contract is a comparison of two season-sum random variables including attrition.

rules_evidence.quote: Dead-heat rules apply in the event that two or more players are tied at the final qualifying position.
rules_evidence.establishes: Top-N rank markets pay 1/N at the cutoff tie, and fantasy scores with 0.1-point increments make ties at the cutoff rare but real for weekly ranks.

rules_evidence.quote: It ranks all WRs, including eligible players without a listed market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Weekly leader contracts are decided over the entire wide-receiver pool, not the listed candidates, so the field's residual mass is part of every listed player's probability.

variants_and_edge_cases: Per-game over thresholds with non-integer strikes (9.2 for a kicker, 34 and 49 'at least' for any-game highs) mix player types: kickers score by field goal distance and extra points, and the sampled rule text is truncated before the kicker scoring table, so kicker weights are unverified.

Season-high contracts (KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH, KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE for rookies) are the maximum of up to 17 single-game scores, and rookie pools combine many players, so they depend on the upper tail of each game's distribution and on availability.

Weekly and positional leader markets (KXNFLFFWEEKLEAD, KXNFLFFWEEKTOP, KXNFLFFLEADER, KXNFLFFLEADERTOP, KXNFLFFPLAYOFFLEADER) rank all players in the group using Sleeper's group membership at expiration; the Weeks 15-17 market sums three games and excludes defence, kickers and IDP.
Season ladders and totals use regular-season games only; the per-game ladder is capped at $1.00 for 100 points, which is rarely binding, and rounding half-up is explicit.

Sleeper's fantasy values are published for the 'full game (including overtime)' and corrections after expiry are ignored, so a late stat correction does not change the settlement even if the league changes the official stat.
contract.settlement_data_source: Sleeper's published fantasy points (default full-PPR) at expiration, with Sleeper determining player group membership; official game stats feed Sleeper but corrections after expiration are ignored.

mechanism.summary: A full-PPR fantasy score is a linear combination of a player's counting stats, and all of the weight is on four components: receptions (one point each), yardage (a tenth of a point per rushing or receiving yard, 0.04 per passing yard), touchdowns (six, with four for a passing touchdown) and negatives (interceptions, lost fumbles). The player must first be on the field; availability and snap share set an atom at zero and a ramp. Opportunity (targets, carries, dropbacks) comes from team volume and role; yield comes from efficiency and matchup; touchdowns come from goal-line and red-zone opportunity with a very large luck component and discrete six-point jumps. Components covary within a player (receptions with yards) and across teammates (a quarterback's touchdown pass is a receiver's touchdown), so total variance is far higher than the sum of marginals suggests. Ranking and leader contracts are order statistics over a whole pool with correlated members, and 'any game' contracts are maxima over a season; the settlement defers to Sleeper's own numbers and group definitions.

stages.name: Participation: active status, snaps and the zero atom
stages.description: The player must be active and on the field; inactive or non-playing players are scored zero by contract. Snap share and role caps (a returning player, a rotational receiver) determine whether he gets opportunities. This stage produces an atom at zero (5-15 percent of player-weeks for those with injury designations) and a ramp.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated: atom at 0 for inactive, ramp for limited players, near-constant for healthy starters.

stages.name: Opportunity volume: targets, carries, dropbacks
stages.description: Team plays and pass rate generate the pool of dropbacks and rushes, and the player's role determines his share; script moves volume toward passing or running by state. Opportunities are strongly overdispersed and are the most predictable part of fantasy points.
stages.distribution: Counts with negative-binomial dispersion; team volume ~ plays 60-70, pass rate 55-60 percent.

stages.name: Yardage and reception yield
stages.description: Receptions earn one point irrespective of yards, so PPR rewards high-volume short-area roles, while yards add a tenth of a point per yard. The yield per opportunity depends on depth, efficiency and matchup, and the PPR reception point makes catch counts, not yards, the stable core of the score for slot receivers and backs.
stages.distribution: Receptions binomial in targets; yards compound; receptions and yards are positively correlated within a player-game.

stages.name: Touchdown scoring: goal-line opportunity and luck
stages.description: Touchdowns are six points each, so one touchdown can equal 60 yards, and they come from goal-line and red-zone usage with a Poisson-like process whose variance dominates fantasy score variance. The expected rate is determined by play-level opportunity location; realised touchdowns are partly luck and regress.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like with mean 0.3-0.8 per game for starters; each touchdown a six-point jump (passing: four points for the quarterback, six for the receiver).

stages.name: Negative events and kicker special case
stages.description: Interceptions, lost fumbles and kicker misses subtract points; quarterbacks carry most of the downside, and kickers' scores are driven by the number of field-goal and extra-point opportunities, which depend on team drives and red-zone stalls. Kicker scoring weights are not shown in the sampled text.
stages.distribution: Low-count events with small penalties; kicker points are discrete sums of 3-5 point field goals and 1 point extra points.

stages.name: Aggregation: component covariance and team stacks
stages.description: The score is the sum of components that move together: a touchdown pass is four points for the quarterback and six for the receiver, shootouts raise every player in the game, and teammates compete for the same carries and targets. This covariance determines the variance of the total, the joint distribution for H2H comparisons and top-N ranks.
stages.distribution: Variance of the score is the sum over components and covariances; positive within a pass-catching stack, negative among backs in the same room.

stages.name: Order statistics: season highs, weekly leaders and position ranks
stages.description: A season-high market is the maximum of the player's remaining single-game scores; a weekly leader is the maximum over the whole position pool; a season leader is a cumulative maximum. Each needs the right tail of the per-game distribution and the field beyond the listed players.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail; maximum of N draws grows with log N; weekly leader of 100+ WRs has expected maximum around 30 points (assumption).

stages.name: Settlement: Sleeper scoring, group definitions and timing
stages.description: Contracts settle on Sleeper's published points at expiration; group membership (WR versus RB, rookie status) is determined by Sleeper, and corrections after expiration are ignored. Differences between Sleeper's settings and other fantasy platforms change the score.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official stats to Sleeper points; settlement risk comes from classification and correction timing.

nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.label: Component and teammate-stack covariance of fantasy points
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.mechanism: Correlation matrix of a player's scoring components (receptions, yards, touchdowns) and between teammates' scores (quarterback-receiver, same-backfield).
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.rationale: Variance of the fantasy total is mostly covariance, and head-to-head, top-N and ladder markets depend on it; a quarterback touchdown pass produces four points for him and six for his receiver, which the sum-of-marginals logic ignores.
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-game data compute the correlation between components within a player and between pairs of teammates, by position pair, after removing team-week means; shrink pairwise correlations to position-pair averages with k=80 games; use a Gaussian or t-copula for joint simulation. Output a correlation matrix per game by team and position and variance multipliers for total scores.
raw_data: player-game components: pass yards, pass TD, rush yards, rush TD, receptions, receiving yards, receiving TD, INT, fumbles lost
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.why: Needed for H2H, top-N and ladder probabilities where correlation changes the answer, and for the shootout effect across a whole game.

nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.label: Play-level expected touchdowns (xTD) from opportunity location
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.mechanism: Sum over a player's carries and targets of the probability that the play scores a touchdown given its yard line, distance to go and air yards.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.rationale: Touchdowns are the largest fantasy variance source and regress strongly; share of red-zone usage alone is a coarse measure, while a play-level expected touchdown count is a direct estimate of true touchdown rate.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.measurement: Fit a logistic model on 2016-2025 plays: P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play type, air yards, role) for carries and targets, then player xTD per game = sum of play probabilities over the last 12 games with half-life 6, shrunk toward position-role mean with k=4 games; forecast = xTD rate x projected opportunities; compare actual TD minus xTD for regression diagnostics.
raw_data: pbp: yardline_100, down, ydstogo, rusher_id, receiver_id, air_yards, touchdown flag
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.why: Provides the touchdown component of a PPR forecast with a play-level calculation that red-zone share and anytime-TD rates only approximate.

nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.label: Sleeper scoring settings, group membership and correction timing
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.mechanism: Mapping from official stats to Sleeper's default full-PPR points, including kicker and bonus rules, the position group each player is assigned to and when Sleeper publishes or corrects totals.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.rationale: The contract settles on Sleeper's number, not on the league's stat; a player's position group (WR/RB/TE/QB), rookie flag, rounding and timing of the published value determine the outcome and cannot be assumed from another fantasy platform.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.measurement: Archive Sleeper's scoring settings (points per yard, per touchdown, per reception, kicker table) and each week's published points at game end, at 24 hours and at settlement; flag differences from the standard stat sheet; keep a table of Sleeper position assignment as of the expiration date; compute a score from official stats and compare with the Sleeper value (error in points).
raw_data: Sleeper player metadata (fantasy_positions), weekly stats, scoring settings
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.why: Defines the target of every contract in the archetype and reduces risk from position classification and corrections, which have no equivalent in the other inputs.

nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.label: Single-game ceiling tail model for any-game highs
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.mechanism: Probability that a player's single-game score exceeds a high threshold (34, 49 points) in a given game, based on per-game distributions with an extreme-value tail.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.rationale: Season-high contracts depend on rare big games rather than the mean; the maximum of 17 games grows with the log of games and is dominated by touchdown clusters and long plays.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.measurement: For each player estimate per-game score distribution with a Poisson-touchdown plus compound yardage model (components from stage s2-s4) and a Pareto tail above the 90th percentile fitted on position-level game scores from 2012-2025; P(max over N remaining games >= x) = 1 - prod(1 - p_g(x)) with p_g adjusted for game-specific total and availability; add an upward correlation correction via nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance. Output P at several thresholds by remaining games.
raw_data: player-game fantasy points history by position
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.why: Directly gives the probabilities for KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH and KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE, which are not threshold events on the mean.

nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.label: Weekly full-pool projection grid and correlation by game
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.mechanism: Projected distribution of fantasy points for every player in a position pool in the week, including bye weeks, inactives and game environment, with shared game effects.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.rationale: Weekly leader and top-5 contracts are decided across the whole pool, so the probability for a listed player depends on how many other strong options play that week, and on shootouts that lift several players together.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.measurement: For each week and position pool (WR, RB, TE, QB) project every player with at least 5 percent of position snap share: mean and variance from the component model, game environment effect from projected total (shared across the game's players), and a probability of inactivity from the injury vintage; simulate 20,000 weeks to compute P(rank = 1) and P(rank <= 5) for each player including ties at the cutoff (1/N).
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.why: Provides a defined field model for the weekly leader contracts whose rules say all eligible players in the group are ranked.

nfl.fantasy_points_model.reason: This is the specification of the aggregation (components times Sleeper weights), not a source of information; keep it tied to nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definitions.

nfl.carries.reason: Carries and goal-line role drive rushing yards and touchdowns, with passing-down role feeding receptions.

nfl.snaps.reason: Snap share bounds opportunity and ramps for returning players; the real participation variable for the zero atom.

interactions.mechanism: Touchdown points equal red-zone opportunities times conversion, and the number of red-zone trips depends on the score path and the team's total; a goal-line back on a high-scoring favourite gets multiplied opportunities, while the same share on a low-scoring team yields little.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress touchdowns on red-zone carries x team expected points and compare to additive models.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback and his top receiver share a touchdown pass, so their fantasy scores are positively correlated and the quarterback's total variance includes the receiver's; for H2H of a quarterback versus a receiver on the same team this correlation lowers the variance of the difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of QB and WR1 fantasy points by team and compare variance of the difference with the independent case.

interactions.mechanism: When a starter is inactive his snaps and carries are taken by the next player on the depth chart, with a larger share to the one with a similar role, so one teammate's absence changes another's expected points non-uniformly by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare backups' snaps and fantasy points in games without the starter, split by role similarity.

interactions.mechanism: In a high-total game several receivers have high scores, so the weekly leader is more likely to come from a shootout, and probabilities across players in the same game are positively correlated; independent field assumptions understate how often one game supplies the leader.
interactions.how_to_test: Check historical share of weekly WR leaders coming from games in the top quartile of totals.

interactions.mechanism: The chance of a 34-point or 49-point game grows rapidly with touchdown count (three touchdowns plus yardage), so the high rungs are driven by the product of goal-line opportunity and big-play rate rather than by mean points.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(34+) conditional on touchdown count and on long-play count; compare to a normal approximation.

interactions.mechanism: The reception point makes PPR value rise with targets, but the marginal value of an additional target falls once the target depth falls and the catch rate drops, so scores grow less than linearly with target share at the top.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress PPR points on target share with a spline and check concavity at the top decile of share.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete six-point jumps: score distribution multi-modal at multiples of 6 plus a yardage base
nonlinearities.why: One extra touchdown moves a score by six points, so the cumulative distribution has steps; threshold probabilities move non-smoothly with the touchdown rate.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: zero if inactive, partial ramp for returning players, near constant for starters
nonlinearities.why: Fantasy output follows snaps closely, and snaps are step-like in injury status, which gives a bimodal distribution around the zero atom.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy right tail with probability of 34+ falling by a factor of 3-4 for each additional 10 points
nonlinearities.why: High fantasy scores come from rare multi-touchdown games, so probabilities for the highest rungs fall much faster than a normal tail with the same variance would predict.

nonlinearities.shape: expected maximum grows with log of pool size and heavy-tailed marginals
nonlinearities.why: The weekly position leader sits far out in the distribution of the pool, so small changes in a player's tail change his leader probability by more than his mean does.

contract.settlement_definition: A heterogeneous set of twenty team and event contracts. Per-game team counts settle on the stated team's total in the full game: field goals (Minnesota 4+), sacks (sacks on 2-point tries excluded), total yards, player rushing attempts (one live play locks in stats), and race-to-points ('Neither team' if nobody reaches 35, overtime included). Season counts and extremes settle on the 2026-27 regular season: number of ties, 60+ yard field goals league-wide, longest win streak, last undefeated team (by week of first loss, ties are not losses, same-week losses tie), fewest or most points scored and allowed (dead-heat), division exact order, worst-to-first, primetime appearances (only scheduled and played national windows) and a voted list (NFL Top 100, players only).

rules_evidence.quote: Any sacks recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The sack count excludes two-point attempts, so only regular plays from scrimmage count and the opportunity pool is dropbacks outside conversion tries.

rules_evidence.quote: If neither team scores 35 points, the Neither Team market resolves Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The race contract is a first-passage event on both teams' cumulative scores with a 'neither' state, including overtime, which makes it a tail event of the joint score path and not a threshold on a single team.

rules_evidence.quote: If the last remaining undefeated teams lose in the same week of the season, they are considered tied for the purposes of this market
rules_evidence.establishes: Resolution is by week of first loss, with ties and bye weeks treated as not-losses, so the contract is a hazard timing problem across teams on a weekly grid rather than an exact-date race.

rules_evidence.quote: The season opener scheduled for Wednesday, September 9 will not be considered a primetime game
rules_evidence.establishes: The count includes only designated national windows (Sunday, Monday and Thursday night, Thanksgiving, Christmas) that were played, so flexible scheduling and the excluded opener determine the count.

rules_evidence.quote: If two or more teams are tied, dead-heat rules apply
rules_evidence.establishes: Fewest points allowed over a season is a min over 32 teams with 1/N sharing at ties, a season-level extreme.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is not started within 48 hours, the market will resolve to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Per-game team counts void to fair price if the game does not start within 48 hours and stay open with a delay inside it, a rule shared by the yards, sacks and field-goal series.

variants_and_edge_cases: Per-game team counts (field goals, sacks, yards, rushing attempts) are 'N+' strikes with half-point floors (3.5, 5.5, 449.5, 8.5) and use the same postponement rule, but KXNFLRSHATT is a player count with the one-live-play activation rule while the team counts have none because the team always plays.

Season-extreme contracts (most ties, 60+ yard field goals, longest win streak, fewest points allowed, worst-to-first, last undefeated) are tail events over 32 teams and 272 games and are governed by league-wide base rates and correlated team strengths, not by a single team's rate.
Ties are not losses (undefeated contracts) but break win streaks, and a tie count of 4+ in a season is a very rare Poisson tail (roughly 0.5 ties per season on average, assumption).

KXNFLT100TOP resolves on a list voted exclusively by active players, KXNFLPRIMETIME on the broadcast schedule, KXNFLMATCHUP and KXNFLSTAGEOFELIM on playoff paths; each belongs to a different mechanism family (voting, scheduling, bracket) than the count process.
Race-to-points and Neither-team contracts include overtime, so overtime possessions add to the opportunity to reach the strike.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in any sampled text (official league statistics and the 'Governing League' schedule and standings are implied); the player-voted list references the league's publication.

mechanism.summary: Two different generating processes sit in this group. For per-game team counts (field goals, sacks, yards, rushing attempts) the outcome is a number of opportunities times a per-opportunity rate: field goals come from drives that stall inside the kicker's range, sacks from opposing dropbacks times a pressure-to-sack conversion, yards from plays times yards per play and rushing attempts from plays times run share, all rewritten by the score path and by weather; the counts are overdispersed and discrete, so thresholds are tail masses of a negative-binomial-like distribution. For season-level specials (ties, win streaks, undefeated runs, fewest points, worst-to-first, long field goals, primetime counts) the outcome is an extreme or timing statistic over 32 teams and a 272-game season, which depends on correlated team strengths, schedule order, and rare base rates. Settlement mechanics (dead heat, week-of-first-loss, designated windows) turn each into a specific functional of the simulated season, and a few contracts (voted lists, scheduling) do not depend on game outcomes at all.

stages.name: Opportunity counts for the team in the game
stages.description: Counts are built on opportunities: plays and dropbacks, drives and stalled drives, rushing plays. The offence's tempo and the opponent's ball control determine how many occur, and overtime adds possessions. For the sack contract the relevant pool is the opponent's dropbacks outside two-point tries.
stages.distribution: Counts: plays ~120-135 combined, drives ~22-26, dropbacks ~35-45 per team; approximately normal with small skew.

stages.name: Field goals: stalled drives inside range and kicker conversion
stages.description: A field goal needs a drive that reaches kicker range and stalls, a decision to kick, and a make. The rate of stalls inside range depends on red-zone efficiency, and the make depends on distance, weather and kicker. Long-field-goal counts depend on the number of attempts beyond 55-60 yards and a steep make-probability curve.
stages.distribution: Count of field goals per team ~1.6 on average (0-5 range), NB-like; make probability falls from 0.95 at 30 yards to 0.35-0.45 at 60+.

stages.name: Sacks, interceptions and the pressure conversion
stages.description: A defence's sacks come from the opponent's dropbacks times the rate at which pressure turns into sacks; interception counts follow dropbacks times a per-attempt rate that regresses toward the mean and rises with pressure and trailing script. Both are low counts with heavy dispersion.
stages.distribution: Sacks per team-game mean ~2.3 (0-8) overdispersed; interceptions mean ~0.7 per team-game, Poisson-like.

stages.name: Yardage, first downs and play-level success
stages.description: Total yards and first downs follow plays and success rate with a per-play yield distribution; drive-level variance makes the totals overdispersed. Penalties and weather shift both rates modestly, and the script changes which play types dominate.
stages.distribution: Total yards per team ~ 330 mean, sd ~ 80; first downs ~ 19 mean, sd ~ 5.

stages.name: Count dispersion and rare in-game events
stages.description: Counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because opportunities and rates are correlated within a game and across stats; rare events (safeties, two-point conversions, ties, overtime) add small masses at the tails of the score path. The model needs a dispersion parameter per stat rather than a Poisson assumption.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial with dispersion parameter that differs by stat; safeties ~1 in 15-20 games; ties ~0.2-0.3% of games.

stages.name: Season-level extremes across 32 teams
stages.description: Longest win streak, last undefeated team, most ties, lowest scoring and fewest points allowed, and worst-to-first outcomes are extremes or hazards over a correlated field of teams. They depend on team strength dispersion, the order of the schedule, byes and ties breaking streaks, and the shared rating uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value structure: P(any team wins 9 straight) depends on p^9 per team-start with correlated strengths; first-loss timing is a hazard on a weekly grid.

stages.name: Scheduling and voted-list contracts
stages.description: Primetime appearances are determined by the published schedule and by flexible scheduling of Sunday and other national windows, which depends on team records and appeal; the Top-100 list is voted by players and depends on ratings, reputation and production, none of which is a game outcome. These contracts require non-game inputs.
stages.distribution: Discrete counts set by the schedule (typically 2-6 national games) with a flex-driven change of 0-2; voted ranks are a noisy function of reputation.

nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.label: Count-statistic dispersion by stat and score-state split
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.mechanism: Negative-binomial dispersion parameters and mean multipliers for field goals, sacks, interceptions, rushing attempts and yards by score state and game total.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.rationale: Thresholds like 4+ field goals or 6+ sacks are tail masses; a Poisson assumption understates them, and dispersion changes with whether the game is a blowout or a close contest.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.measurement: From 2012-2025 team-games fit, per stat, a negative binomial with mean = opportunities x rate and dispersion k by stat and by score-state bucket (lead>=14, within 7, trail>=14); shrink k toward the league-stat value with a gamma prior (equivalent to 200 team-games); output PMF for each stat given expected mean and state mixture over the pre-game margin distribution.
raw_data: team-game counts: field goals made, sacks, interceptions, rush attempts, total yards, with score differential history
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.why: Turns means into tail probabilities for the 'N+' strikes used in the per-game count series.

nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.label: Long field-goal attempt and make model (50+ and 60+ yards), by kicker, venue and weather
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.mechanism: Expected number of attempts of 55+ and 60+ yards and make probability by distance bin for each kicker, adjusted for altitude, roof and wind.
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.rationale: The 60+ yard season contract needs the number of attempts (a coaching and game-state decision, usually at the end of halves) and a steeply falling make probability, both with strong venue and kicker dependence.
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.measurement: Per kicker over his last 3 seasons: make probability by distance bin (50-54, 55-59, 60+) from a logistic regression on distance, altitude, dome and wind with kicker random effect (shrink with k=8 attempts); league attempt rate of 60+ per 100 games adjusted for end-of-half and score state; season expected count = sum over games of attempts x make; for Denver (altitude) add venue multiplier. Output expected count and variance for the league total.
raw_data: pbp: kick_distance, field_goal_result, kicker_player_id, stadium, wind
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.why: Provides the Poisson-like tail for the 8+ league-wide 60-yard field goals market and for per-game field goal thresholds beyond the range effects.

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.label: Win-streak and undefeated-hazard path model across 32 teams
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest win streak, the week of the last first loss, and the number of ties, from a correlated season simulation with shared rating uncertainty.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.rationale: Streak and undefeated contracts depend on the sequence of game outcomes and on strength dispersion, not just on win totals; ties break streaks without being losses, and a bye week is an unrecorded week.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.measurement: Simulate the 272-game season 100,000 times with team ratings (from own rating, with shared draw per team of sd 2.2 points), tie probability 0.25% per game, schedule order and byes; record for each simulation the longest streak (ties break) for each team, the week of each team's first loss (ties not losses), tie count and the worst-to-first indicator using last-year division ranks; output probabilities for each contract rung.
raw_data: schedule order, byes, last-season division ranks, ratings
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.why: Defines the simulation outputs required for six distinct season-extreme contracts in the archetype, which none of the existing inputs provide.

nfl.primetime_flex_probability.label: Primetime window assignment and flex-scheduling probability
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.mechanism: Number of national-window games a team has in the published schedule and the probability that flexible scheduling adds or removes games before the season ends.
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.rationale: The primetime count is a deterministic function of the schedule apart from flex decisions, which depend on team records and appeal and are announced 6 to 12 days ahead; the count of 5+ games is therefore mostly known at release with a flex-driven change.
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.measurement: From the published schedule, count designated national games by team (Sunday, Monday, Thursday night plus Thanksgiving and Christmas, excluding the Wednesday opener); estimate the probability of a flex in/out per eligible week as a logistic function of team record and previous primetime count from 2023-2025 flex rules (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for current flex rules); expected final count = base + sum of flex probabilities; output PMF.
free_sources: NFL schedule releases and flex announcements
raw_data: schedule by team with network window
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.why: The primetime contract has a different information set than game outcomes: it is decided by network scheduling, which no existing input models.

nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.label: Defence sack-count decomposition: opponent dropbacks, pressure rate, conversion
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.mechanism: Expected sacks by this defence equal opponent expected dropbacks times pressure rate times pressure-to-sack conversion, with opposing quarterback's sack avoidance and the offence's pass protection.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.rationale: The 6+ sacks contract is a tail of a thin count; the mean depends on three multiplicative factors with different regression speeds, and the conversion factor is quarterback specific.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.measurement: Expected opponent dropbacks from nfl.pace and nfl.script; team pressure rate over last 12 games (half-life 6, shrink k=120 dropbacks); conversion = sacks / pressures with opposing quarterback's career-regressed rate (shrink k=100 pressures) and pass-rusher availability adjustment; E[sacks] = dropbacks x pressure rate x conversion; add overdispersion from the count model. Needs pressure data or a sack-plus-hit proxy.
raw_data: pbp: sack, qb_hit, qb_dropback, passer, defteam
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.why: Splits the team sack count into three separately estimable factors and brings the opposing quarterback into a defensive count.

nfl.pace.reason: Plays and drives bound all counts, but the opponent's pace and ball control matter as much as own pace.

nfl.drives.reason: Drives are the opportunity base for field goals, turnovers and race-to-points events.

nfl.success_rate.reason: Success rate links to first downs and yards but not directly to the contracts sampled (yards, sacks, field goals); no first-down series is live.

nfl.kicker.reason: Kicker accuracy and range convert stalled drives to field goals and determine long-field-goal counts; needs altitude and wind terms.

nfl.redzone.reason: Red-zone touchdown versus field goal conversion decides the mix at the end of drives; noisy and regressive.

nfl.int_rate.reason: Interception rate regresses; relevant to the next-interception contract and the team interception counts.

nfl.pass_rush.reason: Pressure and sack rate drive the team sack contract; better as a pressure rate with conversion.

nfl.turnovers.reason: Takeaway luck regression matters for interception markets; overlaps int_rate.

nfl.safety_risk.reason: Generic rare-event label without a formula; safeties are a base-rate problem tied to offensive line, punter and field position that the entry does not specify.

nfl.script.reason: Score state shifts dropbacks, sacks and rushing attempts in opposite directions; essential for rushing attempts.

nfl.garbage_time.reason: Garbage-time mass is the tail of the score-state distribution already represented by the script lattice.

nfl.ot_model.reason: Overtime and tie probability gives tie counts and extra possessions; tails matter for the season ties contract.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Wind and cold reduce passing and kicking; used for field goals, sacks and yards.

nfl.penalties.reason: Flag rates change first-down and yards counts; small and not directly connected to the live series.

nfl.officials_crew.reason: Crew penalty tendencies are second-order for the counts in this archetype and have no direct link to season extremes.

interactions.mechanism: Trailing teams throw more and take more hits late, so opposing defences with a lead produce more sacks per dropback, while a leading offence that runs reduces the opposing sack pool; the sign of the script effect on the sack count depends on which team leads.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate sacks per opponent dropback by the defence's score state and quarter.

interactions.mechanism: In high wind or cold the effective range of a kicker falls by several yards, and at altitude it rises; the number of 60-yard attempts and their make rate switch regimes by venue and weather, so the league-wide count is a mixture over venue types.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate 55+ make rates by wind bin and altitude, and attempts by roof type.

interactions.mechanism: Field goals per game equal drives times the chance of stalling in range, which is the complement of the red-zone touchdown rate; a strong red-zone offence produces fewer field goals even with many drives, so drives and red-zone efficiency move the count in opposite directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress field goals per game on drives and red-zone touchdown rate and test the interaction coefficient.

interactions.mechanism: A tie ends a win streak without ending undefeated status, so the streak and undefeated contracts use the same simulation but ties affect them in opposite ways, and the tie probability matters more for the streak contract than for the other.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the simulated probability of a 9-game streak and of a team undefeated at week 12 under tie probabilities of 0 and 0.5 percent.

interactions.mechanism: Flexible scheduling favours teams with good records, so a team that wins early is more likely to receive more primetime games, which correlates the primetime count with the team's success; independence between the schedule and the game results is invalid for flex.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether flex-ins correlate with prior-week record and win percentage.

interactions.mechanism: Count dispersion depends on the score path because blowouts produce both extreme sack and rushing counts; mixing across score states creates fat tails in the marginal count distribution, so the count threshold probability is not that of a single negative binomial.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the mixture of state-specific negative binomials with a single negative binomial on tail frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: steep logistic decay of make probability with distance, especially beyond 55 yards, with altitude shift
nonlinearities.why: A few extra yards cut the make probability by several percentage points, so the 60+ yard count is a nonlinear function of distance distribution and venue.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in per-game win probability: P(streak of 9) scales like p to the power of 9 per start
nonlinearities.why: A team with 0.8 win probability per game has 13 percent per start against 3 percent for a team at 0.67, so a small ratings difference leads to a large streak difference.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed count tail: tail probability rises faster than a Poisson model for a given mean
nonlinearities.why: Over-dispersion increases the mass for 6+ sacks and 4+ field goals, so strikes in the upper tail are underpriced by Poisson assumptions.

nonlinearities.shape: Poisson tail for season ties with very low mean (about 0.5)
nonlinearities.why: A threshold of 4 ties lies far in the tail, so its probability depends sharply on the exact per-game tie probability and the clustering of tight games.
